input.quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
input.rationale: The renewal mechanic sits in the Term clause (Section 13, p0078): the initial term is 1 year and the Agreement renews automatically for successive one-year periods, with either party — including us as Client — able to prevent renewal on written notice given no later than 30 days before the end of the then-current year. On the material terms this meets the preferred position: renewal terms are 12 months (not multi-year), and the non-renewal notice window is 30 days, well inside both the preferred 30-day and fallback 60-day limits, and nowhere near the 90-day walk-away threshold. The notice right is mutual, so it does not operate against us. Two preferred sub-elements are absent and are noted only: there is no Vendor obligation to send a renewal reminder 60 days ahead, and there is no CPI/3% cap on renewal price increases — Section 6 (p0047) only freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds a most-favoured-rate commitment, leaving uplift at renewal uncapped. Under the playbook's classification semantics a missing reminder mechanic and a missing price-uplift cap are minor sub-elements short of preferred wording, so no redline is proposed. If the renewal pricing is negotiated elsewhere, we may raise the uplift cap as a low-priority ask alongside the fee schedule rather than under this rule.
